brief: Goldman desks say the bond selloff is nearing the point where equities start to react. Wednesday's 10-year Treasury yield closed at 5.1079%, a post-2007 high, roughly 5bp from Goldman's threshold for equity pain: a 30bp move over two weeks. Higher oil prices, strong PMI data, hawkish Fed speak, futures selling, convexity paying and a weak 5-year auction drove that move. Fed officials Barr, Paulson, Hammack and Williams reinforced the hawkish tone, and October hike odds moved from 50/50 to about 70% in a day, though Goldman's economists still expect fewer hikes than the market is pricing. Kaplan expects one more hike to roughly 4-4.25% then a pause, attributing the extra pricing to an oil and Fed-chair risk premium. Treasury's own long-end buyback underfilled, and the 5-year auction has tailed 13 of its last 15. AI borrowers SoftBank/OpenAI and CoreWeave are now paying near-10% yields, which Goldman ties to a higher-for-longer case. Equity positioning looks fragile: 45% of S&P names show negative beta, half sit below their 200-day average, and Goldman's Panic Index just posted its biggest one-day drop in a decade, though light positioning could still produce a squeeze higher, not a selloff.
